key_insight: A data-free graph neural network can solve PDEs in solid mechanics by enforcing the weak form with finite-element shape-function gradients instead of automatic differentiation.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a scalable surrogate for FEM that can generalize to new geometries and load cases while avoiding the cost of generating training data.
method: Use message-passing GNNs to predict nodal displacements on FE meshes.
Compute physics residuals from the weak form using polynomial shape-function gradients.
Use the residual as both a training constraint and an inference-time error indicator for refinement.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports residual convergence errors below 1% and successful scaling to large models with arbitrary geometries on unseen cases.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the FE mesh and residual-based refinement may add extra inference cost when the tolerance is not met.
paper_title: Data-free neural PDE solvers based on Graph Neural Networks and weak forms
